$description: The Nithya menu. Every kit, component and pattern you can choose, by category. Themes are read from each kit's token file, so they never go stale here. Browse with `node nithya.mjs`.

categories.kits: A whole design system for one or more runtimes: tokens, themes and components. Pick one per app.
categories.themes: Ready-made looks inside a kit. Choose which ones an app ships, and which comes first (the default).
categories.components: Screen parts in a kit. They come with the kit; this list tells you what you get and where it lives.
categories.patterns: Ideas worth reusing in any app, written up with the code that does them.

kits.name: Studio
kits.summary: Dark-first look for creative tools: launcher cards, a prompt dock, floating panels over a canvas.
kits.origin: Clean-room study of a shipped creative-studio app (docs/clean-room.md).

flutter.label: Flutter
next: Apply a theme:  MaterialApp(theme: nithyaTheme(nithyaPalettes['<first theme>']))
Change tokens in <dest>/tokens/nithya.tokens.json, then run  node <dest>/tokens/build.mjs

react.label: React (Tauri + web)
next: Install the parts' libraries in your app:  npm i react react-dom lucide-react
Change tokens in <dest>/tokens/nithya.tokens.json, then run  node <dest>/tokens/build.mjs

kits.name: Calm
kits.summary: Quiet, readable look for everyday apps: global themes in light and dark, calm motion, a safe theme editor, a '?' on every number.
kits.bestFor: Personal and record-keeping apps where people read more than they make.
kits.origin: Our own design, first built for Arogya Swasthya (2026-10).

svelte.label: Svelte 5
next: Add <dest> to your npm workspaces, then  npm install
In main.ts:  import 'nithya-calm/base.css'  and  ui.start()  from 'nithya-calm'
Put ThemePicker and ThemeEditor on a settings page; every other screen follows
Change tokens in <dest>/tokens/calm.tokens.json, then run  node <dest>/scripts/build.mjs  (Node 22.18 or newer)

components.name: Button
components.summary: Primary, quiet and ghost buttons.

components.name: Stat

components.name: Sparkline
components.summary: Small trend line with an optional usual-range band.

components.name: Segmented
components.summary: Pick one of a few options.

components.name: ThemePicker
components.summary: Live mini previews of every theme, plus light/dark and motion choices.

components.name: ThemeEditor
components.summary: Make, share and load themes with a live preview and a readability check.

components.name: NithyaTheme

components.name: Shell

components.name: Segmented

components.name: SelectTile

components.name: SectionedDialog

components.name: SwitchRow

patterns.name: One switch restyles the whole app
patterns.summary: Attributes on <html> pick the theme; every part reads CSS variables, so one change repaints every screen, cross-faded.

patterns.name: Live previews of other themes
patterns.summary: Any element can carry its own theme attributes, so a picker shows true previews side by side.

patterns.name: Calm mode
patterns.summary: Follows the system 'reduce motion' setting, with a manual override; one attribute stops every animation.

patterns.name: Readable text, checked
patterns.summary: Every theme's text and background pairs meet WCAG 2.2 contrast, checked in the build and live in the editor.

patterns.name: Theme editor that cannot inject code
patterns.summary: Users mix colours, fonts and preset looks; imported themes are validated, never raw CSS.

patterns.name: A '?' on every number
patterns.summary: Plain-words explanations in a popover beside each figure and section.

patterns.name: Rail on desktop, tabs on phones
patterns.summary: One navigation list renders as a side rail or as bottom tabs plus More, with text-style glyph icons.

patterns.name: One token file, two runtimes
patterns.summary: A single JSON generates Dart for Flutter and CSS/TS for the web; --check fails on stale copies.

patterns.name: Glow backdrop
patterns.summary: Soft coloured light behind the page from layered gradients, defined per theme as tokens.

patterns.name: Enter to send, a setting
patterns.summary: A prompt box where the user decides whether Enter sends; Shift+Enter always adds a line.
